intro: A 1950s mainframe ran only one job at a time. Whoever goes first decides how long everyone else waits. Try three methods on the same jobs.

fcfs.name: In order
fcfs.explain: First come, first served, and it runs to the end. Simple and fair in the sense of order - but one long job at the front makes everyone else wait.

sjf.name: Shortest first
sjf.explain: Of the jobs waiting, the shortest runs first, to the end. That gives the lowest average wait - but you have to know how long a job takes beforehand.

rr.name: Round robin
rr.explain: Every job gets a time slice, then the next is up and it queues at the back. Short jobs finish quickly and nobody waits forever - but every switch costs something.

jobs.title: Jobs
jobs.limit: The plan does not draw more than six jobs.

truth: That is exactly what operating systems are for: they decide who computes next - so that people do not have to stand at the counter feeding in jobs one by one.
